target.title: fix(gateway): avoid duplicate launchd restart bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway restart` can create a second gateway on macOS installs where the gateway is managed by a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad`/`KeepAlive`.

The failure mode is easiest to hit from non-Aqua contexts, for example SSH or another background shell on a Mac that also has a console/auto-login user session. The old restart path built the launchd target from the caller UID (`gui/${process.getuid()}`), then ran `launchctl kickstart -k`. If that failed, it fell back to `launchctl bootstrap` for that caller domain.

On multi-GUI-session machines, the running KeepAlive job may actually live in the console user domain, such as `gui/501`. Bootstrapping into a different or racing domain can leave two launchd supervisors alive. The symptom is EADDRINUSE churn around the gateway port, gateway lock contention, and services such as the iMessage host fighting between gateway processes.

## Repro Shape

1. macOS gateway installed as a user LaunchAgent with `RunAtLoad` and `KeepAlive`.
2. The active gateway is supervised in the console/auto-login GUI domain.
3. Invoke `openclaw gateway restart` from SSH or a background/non-Aqua context whose `process.getuid()` target is not the loaded job domain, or while launchd is already relaunching the job.
4. The old path can fall through from failed `kickstart -k` to `bootstrap`, creating a second loaded copy instead of restarting the existing one in place.

## Fix

- Probe launchd with `launchctl print <domain>/<label>` before taking restart action.
- Prefer the actual loaded domain among explicit env, console user, caller UID, and the existing `gui/501` fallback.
- Apply the loaded-domain probe to both restart surfaces that can touch launchd: the external helper in `src/infra/restart.ts` and the actual CLI service restart owner path in `src/daemon/launchd.ts`.
- If the job is already loaded, use `launchctl kickstart -k` and never bootstrap.
- Bootstrap only after `launchctl print` confirms the job is not loaded.
- If bootstrap races with another loader and reports already loaded, retry with `kickstart -k` rather than bootstrapping again.
- Add a post-restart listener-count check on the external helper so duplicate gateway listeners are surfaced as a failed restart instead of triggering another fallback.

This intentionally does not change the internal self-restart path in `process-respawn.ts`; launchd-supervised gateways still exit and let KeepAlive relaunch them there. The in-service LaunchAgent restart path still schedules the existing detached handoff before doing direct launchctl work in-process.

## Evidence

- External helper regression coverage models a loaded launchd job and asserts `triggerOpenClawRestart` runs `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway` followed by `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` call.
- CLI owner-path regression coverage now models `openclaw gateway restart` resolving a loaded console LaunchAgent after a caller-domain miss: `launchctl print gui/777/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl enable gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway`, with no `bootstrap` or `bootout` call.
- The genuinely-unloaded path remains covered separately, so `bootstrap` is still allowed only after `launchctl print` reports not loaded.
- The already-loaded bootstrap race is covered: status `37` now retries with `kickstart -k` and does not attempt a second bootstrap.
- Duplicate post-restart listeners are covered on the external helper: two gateway listener PIDs make the restart result fail with a duplicate-listener detail instead of falling through to another launchd action.
- No live production `openclaw gateway restart` was run while validating this fix, to avoid triggering the duplicate-process bug on the real gateway.

### Live macOS LaunchAgent proof (2026-07-01)

- Ran PR head `fd92beecad95f6a3a0a8a935113db38192d35d9f` on a real macOS user LaunchAgent using a disposable label, `ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, in `gui/501`.
- The disposable job was already loaded before invoking the PR restart helper: `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 1`, `pid = 58095`.
- Invoked `triggerOpenClawRestart()` with `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL=ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof`, `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_DOMAIN=gui/501`, and an unused temp gateway port. It returned:
  ```json
  {"ok":true,"method":"launchctl","tried":["launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof","launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof"]}
  ```
- No `launchctl bootstrap` was attempted for the already-loaded job.
- After restart, `launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr98418-proof` returned `state = running`, `runs = 2`, `pid = 58131`, `last exit code = 0`; the proof worker events showed start -> SIGTERM -> start.
- Production gateway listener on `18789` was unchanged before/after the proof run, and cleanup booted out the disposable LaunchAgent successfully.

## Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/service.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/restart.ts src/infra/restart.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.ts src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts src/daemon/service.test.ts`

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.

target.title: fix(agents): forward agent/session/run identity to tool-result middleware
target.body:
Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
$ # Shape before vs after (mirrors factory construction)
BEFORE {"runtime":"openclaw"}
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts
 ✓ |agents-core| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 ✓ |agents-embedded-agent| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Regression tests assert `createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner` is called
with the full identity object (and falls back to `getSessionId()` when
sessionId is omitted).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenClaw tool-result middleware context lacked agent/session/run identity compared with Codex.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS darwin arm64, worktree `/tmp/oc-106910` on `fix/tool-result-middleware-context`, Node via pnpm vitest.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Standalone context construction proof + `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts` and `tool-result-middleware.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Runner is constructed with agentId/sessionId/sessionKey/runId; 14 extension tests + 25 middleware tests pass.
- **Observed result after fix:** OpenClaw path matches the public `AgentToolResultMiddlewareContext` fields Codex already provides.
- **What was not tested:** Live plugin middleware against a full gateway Discord turn (unit/integration coverage is factory-level).

## Summary

- Thread agentId/sessionId/sessionKey/runId into OpenClaw tool-result middleware context
- Wire from `prepareEmbeddedAttemptAgentSession` and compact
- Regression tests for explicit context and SessionManager fallback

target.title: fix(google-video): cancel unread response body on download error
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response, the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed, causing connection stalls. The fix calls `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic (localhost), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2

target.title: improve(android): move Wear agent, session, and model pickers to Home
target.body:
[AI-assisted]
## What Problem This Solves

Wear OS users currently have to move through separate Agent and Session pages to change conversation context, while the active model cannot be selected from Home. That makes frequent context changes slow and consumes limited space on a round Watch display.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves agent, session, and model selection into three compact previous/next controls on Home, removes the redundant Agent and Session pages, and reduces the main pager to Home/Chat, Voice, and Controls. Model discovery and selection use a capability-negotiated Phone proxy contract and remain bound to the selected session.

## User Impact

Wear OS users can switch agent, session, and model without leaving Home, with fewer pages to swipe through. Existing chat, voice, and control workflows remain available, and unsupported model controls stay disabled with older Phone builds.

## Evidence

> [!TIP]
> ### Real Behavior Proof

>
> - [x] **Environment:** Physical Pixel 10 Pro XL and SM-R945F Watch running ai.openclaw.app with matching debug certificates and the refreshed Phone/Wear APK pair.
> - [x] **Security boundary:** The Phone remained the sole Gateway, authentication, credential, and transport boundary; no token, password, or independent Gateway identity was placed on the Watch.

> - [x] **Home result:** The operator-attested Watch capture shows compact Agent, Session, and Model controls directly on Home with the matched Phone proxy online; Home/Chat, Voice, and Controls remain as the three primary pages.

> - [x] **Proof ownership:** The simultaneous Phone and Watch captures and physical interaction result were supplied and attested by the maintainer; exact-source build, installed-hash, online, i18n, static-analysis, and unit-test evidence was bound locally.
> - [x] **Remaining proof gap:** Mixed-version fallback and state-reset paths are exact-source automated proof rather than a second physical mixed-version recording.

target.title: feat: AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no structured observability for AI safety decisions. Events at the six key boundaries — prompt injection detection, tool policy evaluation, external content consumption, memory context selection, compaction safeguard evaluation, and session start — are either silent or scattered across ad-hoc log lines with no unified pipeline, no plugin subscription API, and no operator-facing query surface. Operators cannot audit AI decisions in production, exporters (OTEL, Prometheus) have no channel to subscribe to safety signals, and plugin manifests have no mechanism to declare or gate permitted event types. Issue #82548 identified this gap; this PR closes it.

## Evidence

**Build — Kali (16 cores / 78 GB RAM, commit b55a4334e0b)**
```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass (22/22 checks; one pre-existing flaky
                      process-management test checks-node-compact-small-4
                      is a signal-race in the test harness unrelated to this PR)
```

**Runtime — all 6 families confirmed through canonical pipeline**

Events verified flowing through `diagnostic-ai-safety-events.ts` ring buffer with host-stamped `trusted=true` on a live Gateway boot:

| Family | Emitter | Verified path |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `external_content.consumed` | `execute()` | `agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `context.assembled` | `attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `auditSummaryQuality()` | `compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

**Architectural fixes in HEAD**
- Fix #1: All safety events route through single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline — parallel dispatcher removed
- Fix #2: `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `startGatewayEventSubscriptions()` before any RPC handlers load — boot-phase events no longer dropped
- Fix #3: `emitAuthorizedAISafetyEvent` exposed via `diagnostic-runtime.ts`; low-level trust-bearing emitter kept internal
- Fix #4: Prometheus `recordDiagnosticEvent` switch no longer handles `ai_safety.*` — exclusively routed through `onAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` subscription to prevent double-counting

---

## Summary

Implements a six-family AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548) with production emitters at real operational boundaries, plugin API surface, OTEL + Prometheus export, Gateway query API, CLI command, and Control UI dashboard.

## Event families and emission points

| Family | Emitter | Location |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `buildAttemptPrompt()` | `agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `runCompactionSafeguard()` | `agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `plugin.load` | `loadPlugin()` | `plugins/loader.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

## Architectural fixes (commit b55a4334e0b)

**Fix #1:** All safety events route through the single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline. Parallel ad-hoc dispatcher removed.

**Fix #2 — plugin provenance binding:** `OpenClawPluginServiceContext` exposes `safetyDiagnostics.emit()`. Emitter is host-stamped at load time with `pluginId`, `origin` (bundled vs external), and `trusted` flag from `entry.origin`. Plugins cannot self-attest trust.

**Fix #3 — full taxonomy coverage:** All 6 families wired at production boundaries. No hollow stubs.

**Fix #4 — Gateway lifecycle init:** `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `server.impl.ts` before `createGatewayStartupTrace()` and before any RPC handlers load. Boot-phase events no longer dropped.

## Build proof (Kali — 16 cores / 78 GB, commit b55a4334e0b)

```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass
```

One pre-existing flaky process-management test (`checks-node-compact-small-4`) fails intermittently upstream and is unrelated to this PR.

target.title: fix(codex): preserve JSONL framing across WebSocket writes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Codex WebSocket transport's handling of valid Writable inputs that split UTF-8 bytes or JSONL records across writes.

The current Codex app-server client writes each complete JSON-RPC record and trailing newline in one `stdin.write()` call. This change is defensive adapter contract hardening rather than a reproduction of a failure in that current caller.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex 0.144.5 uses newline-delimited JSON on stdio and one complete JSON-RPC message per WebSocket text frame. The WebSocket adapter exposes a Writable input, so it must preserve UTF-8 decoder state and JSONL record boundaries across arbitrary writes before producing message-oriented WebSocket frames.

The adapter now incrementally decodes UTF-8, retains incomplete JSONL records between writes, sends each completed record as one WebSocket text frame, and flushes a complete unterminated final record when the Writable finishes.

## User Impact

The current one-write-per-message client path is unchanged. Alternate or future callers using valid split Writable writes no longer receive replacement characters or partial WebSocket frames.

## Evidence

- Contract-level live proof used the exact pinned Codex 0.144.5 Darwin arm64 app-server with isolated localhost state. An `initialize` request was intentionally written through `createWebSocketTransport().stdin` as two byte chunks split after 2 of the emoji's 4 UTF-8 bytes. Codex returned a valid response with id 1.

  ```json
  {
    "codexVersion": "0.144.5",
    "requestMethod": "initialize",
    "utf8Marker": "😀",
    "splitAfterBytes": 2,
    "responseId": 1,
    "responseHasResult": true,
    "isolatedCodexHome": true,
    "transportPath": "OpenClaw Writable bridge to Codex WebSocket app-server"
  }
  ```

- Caller inspection confirmed `CodexAppServerClient.writeMessage()` currently performs one complete JSONL write per message; no production stream pipe or byte-chunk writer was found.
- Direct Codex 0.144.5 contract inspection confirmed stdio JSONL framing and one JSON-RPC message per WebSocket text frame in `codex-rs/app-server/README.md` and the stdio/WebSocket transport implementations.
- Extension-specific test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts`: 1 file passed, 4 tests passed, covering split UTF-8 writes and finalization of an unterminated record.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`: passed.
- Targeted extension `oxlint`: passed for the two transport files and regression test.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`: all 3 changed files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.

target.title: fix(ui): defer remembered camera auto-enable until talk reaches listening
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Post-merge review finding on #110817 (Codex inline P2 / ClawSweeper P1): the remembered camera preference (`talkCameraAutoEnable`) auto-enabled from the `onVideoCapability` callback, which fires after transport construction but before `transport.start()` completes. If microphone startup then fails, the browser has already shown a camera permission prompt for a call that never becomes usable — and the preference stays true, so the prompt repeats on every attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the auto-enable trigger from `onVideoCapability` into the `onStatus` handler, firing only when the session first reaches `listening` (microphone acquired, transport live) while video-capable, keeping the once-per-session guard and the persist-false-on-failure loop breaker. `onVideoCapability` now only records capability for the toggle UI.

## User Impact

Starting a talk call with a remembered camera never touches the camera unless the voice call actually connects; a failing microphone no longer produces repeated camera permission prompts.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.test.ts` — 19 tests pass. New/updated coverage: auto-enable waits for `listening` (no camera call on capability alone), fires exactly once across repeated `listening` callbacks, session erroring before `listening` never touches the camera and leaves the preference unchanged; existing failure-persists-false and preference-off cases updated to the new timing.
- Autoreview (Codex gpt-5.6-sol): clean, "patch is correct (0.95)".
- Addresses https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110817#discussion (Codex P2) and ClawSweeper's P1 timing risk on #110817.

target.title: fix(imessage): prevent duplicate messages after delayed sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an iMessage send could complete through `imsg`'s AppleScript fallback after a private-bridge stall, while OpenClaw reported a timeout to the calling agent. The agent then retried the apparently failed send, producing duplicate messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated send timeout is increased from 150 seconds to 180 seconds. This lets the outer RPC outlive `imsg`'s 150-second bridge deadline plus its fallback verification window, while leaving the 10-second probe timeout unchanged.

This is intentionally a boundary fix rather than a second delivery-verification implementation in OpenClaw. In the observed incident, the delivered rows stored their text in `attributedBody`, so OpenClaw's plain `message.text` recovery path could not reliably identify them. `imsg` already owns that verification.

## User Impact

Users should receive one message instead of duplicates when the private iMessage bridge stalls but the fallback send succeeds.

## Evidence

### Redacted live failure timeline before the fix

One cron session issued three sends of the same text to the same chat:

```text
09:00:33  send request 1 started
09:03:14  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7080 persisted
09:03:19  calling agent retried
09:05:57  OpenClaw reported imsg rpc timeout (send); outgoing row 7081 persisted
09:06:19  calling agent used direct imsg send; outgoing row 7082 persisted
```

Recipient and message text are omitted. The matching timeout and persistence timestamps show that the first two sends completed at the point the 150-second outer timer rejected them.

### Dependency and caller contract

- `imsg` assigns send actions a [150-second bridge deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeProtocol.swift#L28-L39), which its [bridge client enforces](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/IMsgCore/IMsgBridgeClient.swift#L97-L121).
- Auto transport [falls through to AppleScript after a bridge error and then verifies the persisted send](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/RPCServer%2BHandlers.swift#L271-L320).
- The persisted-message verifier [polls for up to 8 seconds](https://github.com/openclaw/imsg/blob/ca91c41b47e0bbe75b6ac599b583531ff9fa67d2/Sources/imsg/SentMessageVerifier.swift#L13-L26).
- OpenClaw selects the dedicated default in [`sendMessageIMessage`](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L720-L725) and [passes it to the single RPC request](https://github.com/omarshahine/openclaw/blob/fce7399810c/extensions/imessage/src/send.ts#L871-L885). OpenClaw does not retry this request internally; the calling agent retried after receiving the ambiguous timeout.

### Deterministic delayed-boundary proof

The focused regression test models `imsg` returning successfully at 158 seconds, after the old outer deadline but within the new one. It asserts that the send resolves with the fallback message GUID and that OpenClaw makes exactly one RPC request.

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       52 passed (52)
```

Command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/send.test.ts`

### Live patched-build proof

The branch was rebased onto current `main`, built, and run through Lobster's exclusive iMessage dev-gateway proof workflow. A temporary copy of the morning context-question cron was triggered once with an explicit private destination:

```text
status:          ok
duration:        5207 ms
deliveryStatus:  delivered
database rows:   1
row:             7086 at 10:58:38 local time
```

The recipient, message text, and GUID are omitted. The unique output persisted as exactly one outgoing row. This live run completed through the normal fast bridge path; the 158-second fallback boundary is covered deterministically above because forcing a real bridge stall would require restarting Messages with a stale readiness marker and would introduce an avoidable delivery race.

After proof, the temporary dev cron was removed, the dev gateway stopped, and production was restored healthy on port 18789 with exactly one `imsg rpc` process.

Additional validation:

- Full branch build passed on current `main`.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final Codex branch autoreview: no findings; patch rated correct with 0.94 confidence.

AI-assisted: diagnosis, implementation, test updates, and independent review were performed with Codex under maintainer supervision.

## What Problem This Solves

MiniMax API-key configurations were forcing the Anthropic transport to send an `Authorization: Bearer` header. The official MiniMax Anthropic-compatible endpoints require the API key in `X-Api-Key`, so affected requests failed with HTTP 401 after upgrading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MiniMax API-key provider catalog and onboarding path now leave the Anthropic SDK's standard `X-Api-Key` authentication active, while the separate MiniMax Portal OAuth provider continues to use Bearer authentication.

A plugin-owned Doctor compatibility migration repairs previously written MiniMax API-key configurations for the official global and China endpoints. It is idempotent and deliberately preserves Portal OAuth, custom endpoints, and configurations that are already correct.

## User Impact

Users of the official MiniMax API-key endpoints can send model requests again without manually editing their provider configuration. Existing affected configurations are repaired by `openclaw doctor --fix`.

Closes #110763

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/minimax` — 151 tests passed, including provider catalog, onboarding, Portal OAuth preservation, and Doctor migration coverage.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts -t "uses X-Api-Key for MiniMax API-key provider transport requests"` — the focused request-header test passed in both configured agent test projects. target.title: fix(ui): use clipboard fallback in setup wizards
target.body:
[AI-assisted] ## What Problem This Solves The model and channel setup wizards call the async Clipboard API directly. target.title: fix(ui): stream-decode terminal startup UTF-8 chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI terminal startup input used a module-level `TextDecoder` and called
`decode(bytes)` without `{ stream: true }`. Before a Gateway session is bound,
pasted CJK/emoji can arrive as UTF-8 split across WebSocket/libterminal chunks.
Without stream mode, a mid-sequence chunk becomes U+FFFD mojibake in the
pending input buffer.

An earlier revision incorrectly flushed the decoder on session adoption, which
could finalize a partial scalar as U+FFFD when the completing byte arrived
after bind. This revision keeps the decoder open across adoption and only
flushes on tab dispose.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Decode each chunk with `{ stream: true }`
- Keep decoder state across session adoption (drain buffer only)
- Flush only on dispose
- Regression: bind between bytes of one UTF-8 scalar (`E4 B8` then `AD` → `中`)
- Negative control: non-stream decode of the same split produces U+FFFD

## User Impact

**Before:** Pasting CJK/emoji while a terminal tab is still connecting could
corrupt characters that straddled chunk boundaries (and an adopt-time flush
could make that worse).

**After:** Split UTF-8 sequences reassemble across pre-bind and post-bind
chunks; incomplete trailers flush only when the tab is disposed.

## Evidence

- Changed: `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.test.ts`,
  `ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel.ts`
- Production path: Ghostty `onData` → `createTerminalStartupInput.onData`
  (`decode(..., { stream: true })`) → pending buffer → `adoptSession` drain
  (decoder stays open) → later `onData` completes scalar → Gateway `input`

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. Byte-split UTF-8 for `中😀` reassembles with no U+FFFD before session bind.
2. Session bind between `E4 B8` and `AD` still yields `中` (decoder not flushed).
3. Non-stream `TextDecoder` on the same split produces U+FFFD (negative control).

### Canonical reachability path

`createTerminalStartupInput.onData` → streaming `TextDecoder` →
`BoundedBuffer` / live `connection.input` after `getSessionId()` becomes set →
`adoptSession` drains complete buffer text only → dispose calls `flush()`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses the platform `TextDecoder` stream contract; no new deps.

### Real environment tested

Local trusted checkout exercising the production `createTerminalStartupInput`
helper used by `terminal-panel.ts` (same `onData` / adopt / dispose seams).
Node v22.23.1; PR head `e26c948b840`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-startup-input.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ reassembles UTF-8 code points split across WebSocket chunks before session bind 1ms
✓ does not emit U+FFFD for a mid-sequence chunk without stream mode regression 0ms
✓ keeps decoder state across session bind so a straddling scalar completes 0ms
✓ proves non-stream decode mojibakes the same split that stream mode keeps intact 0ms
✓ flushes incomplete trailer only on explicit dispose flush 0ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Observed result after fix

- One-byte-per-chunk feed of `中😀` drains as exactly `中😀`.
- Bind between `E4 B8` and `AD` delivers `中` to `connection.input`, not `�`.
- Non-stream decode of the same split contains U+FFFD and is not `中`.

### What was not tested

Manual Control UI paste against a live Gateway terminal session / Crabbox
recording. The production helper + panel adopt/dispose seams are covered above.

### Fix classification

target.title: fix(matrix): journal inbound events before advancing sync token
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix loses inbound user messages when the gateway crashes or restarts while an agent turn is running.

The loss window is structural: matrix-js-sdk's `doSync` sets the sync token **before** processing the batch's events ("set the sync token NOW *before* processing the events … so if something barfs on an event we can skip it" — `node_modules/matrix-js-sdk/lib/sync.js:725-728`). The plugin's `SqliteBackedMatrixSyncStore.setSyncData` then persists that token (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/file-sync-store.ts:227-232`, 250 ms debounce). Meanwhile the SDK bridge re-emits the event synchronously (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts:2073-2086`) and the monitor dispatched it **detached** into a memory-only `KeyedAsyncQueue` (`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:539`) for the full agent-turn duration.

So the sequence was: message arrives → token advanced in memory → next `/sync` tells the homeserver the batch is consumed → token persisted to SQLite — all while the message still sits in a memory-only queue. Any crash in that window (routinely minutes, the whole agent turn) permanently loses the message. The existing persistent inbound deduper only stores dedupe records, not the payload, so nothing can replay it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same crash window the durable-ingress fleet adoption (#109657) already closed on the sibling channels — telegram (#108924), discord (#110274), whatsapp (#110418), mattermost (#110386), msteams (#110357), slack (#109910), signal (#109907), imessage (#110409), sms (#109866) — and Matrix is the remaining sync-loop channel still on detached in-memory dispatch. This PR mirrors the merged Mattermost adapter (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-ingress.ts`) one-for-one, mapped onto Matrix's ack equivalent (the sync-token persist instead of a websocket receive):

- New `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.ts`: every dispatchable inbound event (room message, decrypted message, reaction) is journaled into the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue **synchronously inside the sync event listener**. The queue's SQLite write is a synchronous transaction (`src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts` `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`), so the journal row commits in the same macrotask cycle — before the 250 ms-debounced token persist can tell the homeserver the batch is consumed. Durable-before-ack.
- Dispatch now runs through the core durable ingress drain (`createChannelIngressDrain`) with per-room lanes (`room:<id>`, matching the handler's existing per-room serialization), the canonical `turnAdoptionLifecycle` seam (`bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions` → `core.channel.inbound.run`, so the claim tombstones at adoption when the turn's recovery state is durable), bounded retry with backoff and dead-letter (8 attempts / 24 h, shared defaults), and startup replay of journaled rows.
- Handler failures now propagate to the drain when journaled (the detached path swallowed them) so the retry/dead-letter policy owns them; terminal non-turn outcomes (policy gates, dedupe skips) tombstone on dispatch return. The pre-existing persistent deduper keeps homeserver redeliveries exactly-once on top of the drain's tombstones.
- Events without an `event_id` cannot be journaled and keep the previous live-dispatch path (`onUnjournaledEvent`), matching the handler's existing fail-open dedupe behavior for unidentifiable events.
- Journal-append failure retries (0/100/300 ms) then drops loudly (fail closed), mirroring the whatsapp landing decision; because the journal and the sync-token store share the same state DB, a broken DB fails the token persist too, so the homeserver redelivers after restart.
- Shutdown stops ingress after `drainPendingDecryptions` (those emissions still need the journal) and awaits in-flight drain dispatches exactly where the old detached-task `waitForIdle` stood.

No SQLite schema change (reuses the existing `channel_ingress_events` table in the shared state DB), no new config or env surface, no core/SDK changes — the adapter only consumes the already-exported seams (`createChannelIngressDrain`, `bindIngressLifecycleToReplyOptions`, `state.openChannelIngressQueue`).

Known boundary (follow-up candidate, out of scope): E2EE events are journaled when the decrypt bridge emits the decrypted event; a crash between token persist and decryption still loses the still-encrypted event. Closing that needs re-injecting raw encrypted events into the crypto pipeline on replay, which is a separate design.

## User Impact

- A gateway crash/restart during (or before) an agent turn no longer permanently loses Matrix room messages, decrypted messages, or reactions: journaled events replay once on startup and are deduped against already-handled ones.
- Handler failures retry with bounded backoff and dead-letter loudly instead of vanishing into a detached-task log line.

| token persisted | `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/file-sync-store.ts:227-232` | homeserver may consider batch consumed after 250 ms debounce |

target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`

## Evidence

target.title: fix(status): hydrate thinking catalog for Ollama status card surface
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generic text status paths (WhatsApp `session_status` / `/status`) called `resolveSupportedThinkingLevel` without a model thinking catalog.

For live-discovered Ollama models with `reasoning: true`, an active session `thinkingLevel: high` remapped to **Think: off** even when **Reasoning: high** was correct (issue #108337).

This PR hydrates configured-then-runtime catalog metadata before the remap (same idea as runtime `/think` catalog resolution on Telegram/Slack/Discord native menus), so generic status surfaces preserve `Think: high` for discovered reasoning models.

## Differential value

Small status-path fix only. Does not rework channel-native menus (already fixed for TG/Slack/Discord). Adds a WhatsApp-oriented regression for Ollama catalog `reasoning: true` + session `thinkingLevel: high`.

Status rendering never triggers provider discovery: `resolveStatusThinkingCatalog` reads the in-memory `cacheOnly` snapshot first (side-effect-free), then falls back to `readOnly: true` persisted catalog (also discovery-free), and degrades to the configured catalog on any error — so a cache miss or slow/unavailable provider can never delay or fail a status response.

## Evidence

- `npx vitest run src/status/status-text.test.ts` — all 12 tests pass, including the new Ollama WhatsApp status catalog regression (`buildStatusText thinking catalog`), which drives a discovered Ollama reasoning model (`glm-5.2:cloud`, `reasoning: true`) through the real WhatsApp status render and asserts `Think: high` is preserved and never remaps to `Think: off`.
- This regression reproduces the exact #108337 symptom (runtime-discovered Ollama reasoning models losing their thinking level on the status surface) and fails on `main` before this patch.
- Since the output is a text status card with no visual UI surface, the test assertion is the observable behavior; there is no separate screenshot artifact to capture. Redacted live WhatsApp + Ollama runtime output would need a maintainer/reporter with that provider setup.

- `src/status/status-text.ts`
- `src/status/status-text.test.ts`

target.title: fix(heartbeat): remove dead single-line HTML comment checks in isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` in the heartbeat module contained three unreachable `/^<!--.*-->$/` checks, adding unnecessary maintenance burden. The `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` preprocessing step called at the top of the function strips leading HTML-comment scaffolding from each line before the loop body runs, so none of the inline checks can ever match.

The inline checks were introduced across two separate PRs (#86627 and #90431) whose authors both saw existing inline HTML-comment checks in the loop and naturally added more on top, not realizing those checks were themselves unreachable. The root cause is a structural overlap in responsibilities: the preprocessing layer and the loop body both claim ownership of HTML comment handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rather than leave dead code with a comment warning future readers not to touch it, this PR removes all three unreachable checks and adds a single comment at the preprocessing call site explaining the division of labor — `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` (leading-only) owns HTML-comment stripping, and the loop body does not repeat them.

This aligns `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` with the pattern already used by `parseHeartbeatTasks`, which calls the same preprocessing function and has never had inline HTML-comment checks in its loop — confirming the pattern works correctly.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact. This is a dead-code removal with zero behavioral change.

## Evidence

- **Formal proof**: The `stripLeadingHtmlCommentScaffolding` while-loop condition (`state.inHtmlComment || remaining.trimStart().startsWith("<!--")`) guarantees that on loop exit, the output does not start with `<!--`. Therefore `/^<!--.*-->$/` can never match on the trimmed result after preprocessing.
- **Brute-force validation**: 10,000 randomly generated strings containing `<!--` at random positions were tested — zero produced a line matching `/^<!--.*-->$/` after preprocessing.
- **All existing test cases pass**: 32 tests in `heartbeat.test.ts` + 5 tests in `workspace-templates.test.ts` — all green with no modification.
- **Real behavior proof** — live validation using the actual production source (`npx tsx` loading `src/auto-reply/heartbeat.js` directly):

```
=== Modified isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty behavior ===

  [PASS] single-line HTML comment (bundled template)
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] multi-line HTML comment
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] commented-out tasks block
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] two HTML comments on one line
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] comment then header
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] text before inline comment (not scaffolding)
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] plain HTML comment
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] HTML comment then header
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] header only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] actionable list item
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] empty string
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] whitespace only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] fence opener
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] fenced content with task
         expected: false, got: false
  [PASS] empty list item stub
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] headers only
         expected: true, got: true
  [PASS] mixed content with prose
         expected: false, got: false

=== After stripHeartbeatHtmlComments: can /^<!--.*-->$/ match? ===

  No matches — all three removed inline checks were dead code.
```

target.title: fix(reef): stop leaking the inbox loop across channel crash restarts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The live `clawd` gateway's Reef channel was stuck in a self-sustaining relay rate-limit storm: 2,400+ `reef inbox connection failed` errors and ~140 `rate_limited` channel crash/restart cycles per day, with `code=1012 reason=replaced by newer connection` closes every ~600ms during bursts. Inbound delivery from peers (e.g. `molty`) was effectively dead while the relay 429'd every request, including WebSocket handshakes.

Root cause chain:

1. `reefPlugin.gateway.startAccount` ran `Promise.all([inbox.start(ctx.abortSignal), reconciliationLoop()])`. When the 30s friend-reconcile loop threw (e.g. a transient relay 429 → `ReefRelayError("rate_limited")`), `Promise.all` rejected and the channel exited — while `inbox.start()` kept running in the background.
2. The core channel supervisor (`src/gateway/server-channels.ts`) never aborts the crashed task's `AbortController` before starting the replacement (it only aborts on manual stop). The orphaned inbox loop therefore reconnected forever.
3. Orphan and replacement fight over the single per-handle relay inbox socket (`1012 replaced by newer connection`), each completed catch-up resets the reconnect backoff to 250ms, and the resulting connect storm drives the relay into rate limiting — which crashes the next reconcile, leaks another loop, and sustains the storm indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `extensions/reef/src/channel.ts`: new `runReefChannelLifecycle` owns one abort scope for both account loops. Any exit path aborts the inbox loop and awaits its settlement before `startAccount` settles, so no reconnect loop can outlive its account instance. It also inherits an already-aborted parent signal (listeners added after abort never fire). Periodic reconcile failures are now logged and retried instead of crashing the channel — the crash-restart cycle was itself the rate-limit amplifier.
- `src/gateway/server-channels.ts`: defense-in-depth for every channel plugin — the supervisor aborts the settled task's controller before starting a crash replacement (both restart paths) and on terminal cleanup, so two account instances can never share a live lifetime.

## User Impact

Reef channels no longer melt down into relay rate limiting after a single transient reconcile failure; inbound agent-to-agent delivery stays up. Any channel plugin that leaves background work racing on its abort signal after a crash is now cut off by the supervisor before the replacement starts.

## Evidence

- Live diagnosis on the affected gateway: 2,404 inbox failures / 141 `rate_limited` exits on 2026-07-18 (1,109 replacements the prior day), 1012-replacement bursts at ~600ms cadence, escalating to WS handshake 429s.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef` — 24 files, 263 passed / 2 skipped (includes new lifecycle tests: reconcile-failure containment, teardown-before-settle, already-aborted parent inheritance).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` — 51 passed (includes new "aborts the crashed task's signal before starting its replacement").
- Autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): clean after addressing one finding (already-aborted parent signal inheritance).

target.title: fix(scripts): restore Testbox lease claims to the originating repo after delegated runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every delegated Blacksmith Testbox run through `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs` executes the crabbox binary from a throwaway sparse-sync checkout, and crabbox stamps the retained lease's claim sidecar (`state/claims/<tbx_id>.json`) with that temporary cwd. The next `run --id <tbx_id>` from the real repo then fails the ownership guard with "lease is claimed by repo …/crabbox-sync-…; use --reclaim", forcing `--reclaim` on literally every lease reuse. This taxed every proof cycle in recent sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repair the post-run artifact instead of weakening the pre-run guard: after the delegated child finishes (success, failure, signal, or spawn error — hooked into the wrapper's shared `cleanupOnce` path beside the existing temp-artifact reconciliation), if the claim still points at the wrapper's own temp checkout, rewrite `repoRoot` back to the originating repo. Foreign claims (a genuinely different repo) are untouched, every other claim field is preserved, and the write is atomic (temp + rename) with a pre-rename recheck so a concurrent claim update wins. Claim-path resolution is shared with the existing guard helper instead of duplicated, honoring `XDG_STATE_HOME` identically.

## User Impact

Maintainer tooling only: kept Testbox leases are reusable from the originating repo without `--reclaim` after every delegated run. The ownership guard for genuinely foreign repos is unchanged.

## Evidence

- New tests in `test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts`: delegated-run claims pointing at the child checkout are restored to the originating repo on success and failure with other fields preserved; genuinely foreign claims stay untouched.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxv5fskbxxvvaj6b2ssgsnhp`: `pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts` — pass (full wrapper suite incl. the new cases).
- `node --check scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs` clean; `pnpm check:changed` green on the same lease (see checks).
- Bug reproduced repeatedly today: warmup from a repo worktree, next `run --id` from the same worktree refused with the claim pointing at `openclaw-crabbox-sync-7X71De`/`-UA95Nc` temp checkouts.

target.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold
target.body:
Closes #106231

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and reviewed this change under contributor direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent that reached the critical tool-loop threshold would only emit a warning and continue running. The run could keep consuming tokens or repeating tool side effects until a separate timeout or limit stopped it, including through the embedded, Codex, and Copilot harness paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed critical-loop signal now flows from the detector through each harness to one run-terminal owner. That owner stops the active attempt, preserves an earlier user or plugin cancellation, returns the normal blocked-run result, and leaves the session available for the next user turn. Codex native-hook outcomes are also relayed back to loop detection, while duplicate native/managed observations are idempotent by tool-call identity.

## User Impact

Critical tool loops now stop the current run at the configured critical threshold instead of continuing indefinitely. Existing warning thresholds, ordinary tool failures and retries, explicit cancellation precedence, and subsequent use of the same session remain intact.

## Compatibility

This adds no new configuration or storage surface.

The existing Codex `loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` switch currently governs the paired loop-detection relay path: setting it to `false` disables both the loop-only `PreToolUse` marker and its companion `PostToolUse` outcome relay. The outcome relay only completes loop history created by the matching pre-tool observation, so retaining it alone would not provide an independent detection capability. No separate PostToolUse-only setting is introduced.

This does not disable relays required by plugin hooks, trusted-tool policy, or result middleware. The reference and troubleshooting documentation state the paired opt-out explicitly.

**Maintainer decision requested:** Please confirm whether the existing `false` value must preserve its historical PreToolUse-only opt-out, or whether it is now the supported opt-out for the paired PreToolUse/PostToolUse loop-detection path. The current implementation uses the paired behavior. If the historical narrow contract must be preserved, I will adjust the implementation and focused configuration tests before merge. After that decision, I will refresh the final branch against current `main` and rerun exact-head CI.

## Evidence

### Redacted runtime proof

Runtime proof was executed at `c7ca0bd6403e138e4c00b7eb11fdf5d8d842f69b` in an isolated temporary home/state/workspace against a local loopback OpenAI Responses stub. It used no AWS service, external model, external credential, or user data. Current exact head `19d9e8da730a29375d4b091f9652b104feb27c1e` is a patch-preserving rebase onto `3fd3ad83014897ead39d394d8d72b25bfe2f3f83`: both commit patch IDs are unchanged, upstream touched none of this PR's files at the rebase point, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

The embedded OpenClaw CLI returned the following machine-readable outcome, then accepted a second turn with the same session id:

```text
planned read calls = 3 (3 unique call ids)
blocked text       = CRITICAL: Called read with identical arguments and identical outcomes 2 times. Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops.
livenessState      = blocked
error.kind         = hook_block
replayInvalid      = true
blocked session    = <same-session-id>
recovery text      = RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK
recovery session   = <same-session-id>
```

A QA Lab runtime-pair scenario then exercised a real gateway child and qa-channel/qa-lab lifecycle for both `openclaw` and Codex app-server runtimes. Both cells passed. Each persisted one session across two user turns, issued exactly three unique `read` calls, completed the first two, blocked the third at `criticalThreshold=2`, and returned `RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK` on the later turn in the same session. Codex recorded the third tool result as `isError=true` with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.`

The Codex cell exercises both the managed dynamic-tool bridge and Codex's native Pre/PostToolUse path: dynamic tools implement the default `CoreToolRuntime` hook payloads, and the registry runs those hooks around the call ([Codex dynamic handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), [Codex registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)). Blocking on call 3 rather than call 2 is behavioral end-to-end evidence that duplicate managed/native outcome observations were deduplicated; focused tests additionally assert the callback-level idempotence.

The proof-only mock trigger and QA scenario remained uncommitted in the disposable proof checkout. No raw transcript, local path, session UUID, token, or generated state database is attached here.

### Deterministic and review proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.critical-tool-loop.test.ts`: 7/7 passed. This covers sticky critical ownership, backend cancellation rejection, caller cancellation before and after critical detection, plugin abort before a late critical signal, and canonical blocked bookkeeping.
- Focused coverage also covers threshold signaling, outcome ordering, duplicate native/managed observations, persistence, session adoption, usage/replay bookkeeping, Codex managed/native hooks, `/btw`, and the Copilot bridge.
- Two independent source audits found no actionable defects after the cancellation, native-hook, side-question, and deduplication edge cases were addressed.
- Two fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted` passes found no accepted/actionable findings; the latest result was `overall_correctness: patch is correct` with confidence `0.97`.
- Exact-head GitHub Actions passed the authoritative `openclaw/ci-gate`, build, production types, lint, docs, security, all four QA Smoke profiles, and every changed-surface test. No current required check is failing.

### Dependency contract

Non-idempotent command side effects can re-execute when a durable ingress row replays in the crash window between the side effect and its completion tombstone.
